reference_status: Provisional human baseline pending independent practitioner review
method: Human review of every record, grouping recurring problems and retaining contradictory or qualifying evidence.

independent_review.rule: Do not silently change this reference after review. Record agreements, disagreements and any proposed revision separately before deciding whether to version the reference.

themes.problem_statement: Finance users spend substantial time reconciling payment data with bank and accounting records, while exceptions, refunds and shared investigations make discrepancies difficult to resolve.
themes.opportunity_boundary: Help users identify and investigate exceptions while preserving review and approval; the evidence does not support fully autonomous reconciliation.

themes.theme: Delayed visibility of failed or pending payments
themes.problem_statement: Administrators and managers often discover failed or pending payments late, sometimes only after a customer contacts them, and need clearer status, reasons and proactive alerts.
themes.opportunity_boundary: Surface actionable exceptions and status history; do not infer that all payment-status information is unclear.

themes.problem_statement: Teams need a clearer record of payment events and customer communications to avoid duplicate reminders and answer disputes or status questions consistently.
themes.opportunity_boundary: Improve history and traceability without treating isolated receipt-branding requests as a core problem.

notes: Theme boundaries overlap because a single feedback record can support more than one customer problem.
The reference is a documented human judgement, not objective ground truth.
The third theme is specifically subject to independent review because several supporting records also fit the broader payment-status problem.
Future reviewers should record disagreements rather than silently changing the reference.
